# ui::ParallelLayout

Header: `winui/ui/ParallelLayout.hpp`.

How [Window::layout()](window.md#layout) may spread measuring over worker threads ([Window::set_parallel_layout()](window.md#set_parallel_layout)).

Only a batch of siblings whose whole subtrees answer [Element::parallel_measure_safe()](element.md#parallel_measure_safe) goes to the workers, and only when it is large enough to pay for the hand-off. Everything else is measured on the UI thread. The sizes are the same, bit for bit, either way.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Window window{{.title = "Report"}};
window.set_parallel_layout({.enabled = false}); // everything on the UI thread
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Whether to measure on worker threads at all. On by default. Below `min_elements` nothing changes, and above it a form with real text measurement lays out about three times faster (the docs' layout page has the numbers). |
| `min_elements` | `std::size_t` | `256` | The smallest batch worth sending to workers, counted in elements across the siblings' subtrees. A smaller one is measured on the calling thread. |
| `scheduler` | `Scheduler*` | `nullptr` | The pool to measure on, borrowed. It must outlive every layout pass that uses it. nullptr uses the process-wide layout pool, created on first use, with one worker fewer than there are hardware threads and at most 7, since the UI thread measures a share itself. A `Scheduler{Scheduler::Inline{}}` measures everything on the calling thread, through the same batching code. |
